# R2 and the limits that bound attachments

Retrieved 2026-11-23 from the current docs. Not a manual.

## Sources

- https://developers.cloudflare.com/r2/platform/limits/
- https://developers.cloudflare.com/r2/objects/upload-objects/
- https://developers.cloudflare.com/r2/api/workers/workers-api-reference/
- https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/platform/limits/
- https://developers.cloudflare.com/durable-objects/platform/limits/

## What this repo uses

Workers binding `R2Bucket` on `env.ATTACHMENTS`:

- `put(key, value, { httpMetadata: { contentType } })` stores one object. A 25 MB body is a single `put` (single-part limit is 5 GiB; the object limit is 5 TiB).
- `get(key)` returns the object or null. `arrayBuffer()` reads it back. The Worker serves those bytes; the bucket is not public.
- `delete(key)` removes one object. Keys are `{tenant}/{channel}/{uuid}` and stay under the 1,024-byte key limit.

## Limits that decided the shape

- SQLite in a Durable Object: a string, BLOB or row is at most 8 MB. A 25 MB file cannot be a row.
- Incoming request body: 100 MB on Free and Pro zones, 200 MB on Business. Ten 25 MB files (250 MB) do not fit in one request on the zone this Worker uses.
- Worker memory is 128 MB. The upload path keeps one file in memory, then stores it, then reads the next.
- R2 allows one write per second to the same key. Keys are new UUIDs, so a retry that dedupes does not write the same key twice.
